new_public_evidence.source: Larsson, Ramdas & Ruf, The numeraire e-variable and reverse information projection
new_public_evidence.result: For a point alternative against any composite null a numeraire e-variable exists and is log-optimal. Section 7 proves the universal-inference factor q/p_max is pointwise dominated by the numeraire q/p* and is generally inadmissible for a nondegenerate composite null.

new_public_evidence.source: Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen, Safe Testing
new_public_evidence.result: Conditional e-values multiply safely under optional continuation, so a frozen-reference numeraire block factor would retain the existing blockwise sequential semantics if its conditional e-validity is established.
Retained as the finite-sample composite-null baseline for the current r85 q_R/sup_C p block factor.

derived_results.claim: The r85 NIG numerator and Gaussian confidence-set denominator are exactly location-scale equivariant. After z=(Y-Xbar_R)/s_R, every reference maps to one fixed standardized NIG predictor and one fixed null rectangle with h0=0.10582811900240735, ell0=0.9345871297300398 and u0=1.074513925626049. This removes per-reference optimization from the continuum certification problem.

On a new common-random exact-KL=1 Gaussian grid using conservative A=0 delayed-start tail initialization, r85 materially reduced worst q90 delay relative to r82/r84. Worst q90 raw delays at prechange ages 0/1024/10240/98304/1e6 were r82: 96/128/192/224/225.6, r84: 64/120.8/152/176/192, r85: 48/64/96/96/96; every tested scenario detected within 2048 post-change samples. A separate 16,500 paired path-scenario stream had r85 earlier/equal/later than r84 in 4268/12199/33 cases and earlier/equal/later than r82 in 10395/6105/0.

Conditional on frozen R, the r85 problem is exactly a point predictive alternative q_R versus a composite Gaussian null P_R. The numeraire theorem therefore applies blockwise. Any exact numeraire factor uses only R and the current deterministic block, so all delayed starts still share one multiplier and the O(1) telescoping start-mixture recursion survives. The numeraire is pointwise no smaller than r85 universal inference.

Standardization makes the numeraire search reference-independent. A symmetric four-corner Gaussian mixture p_rho on the standardized null rectangle was found with rho about 0.55441744 on the low-variance corner pair and 1-rho on the high-variance corner pair. High-order deterministic hierarchical NIG quadrature solves the low/high active-pair first-order conditions at one and gives expected log evidence about 5.04957 nat/block versus 4.00667 for universal inference, about +1.04289 nat/block under q. Dense search and differential evolution put the continuum constraint maximum numerically at the four corners, but no interval/analytic continuum proof exists yet.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The new matched detector experiment is a conservative post-change tail-state stress, not the full detector distribution after a long null prefix and not evidence about false-alarm probability.

The four-corner mixture is not yet certified e-valid over the whole Gaussian null rectangle; do not call it the RIPr or numeraire until C(mu,sigma)<=1 is proved or a verified epsilon scaling is applied.
High-order quadrature, Monte Carlo and differential evolution are engineering/numerical evidence, not directed-rounding continuum certification.
r85 remains strong but still lacks a full machine/continuum KL>=1 power certificate.
All results remain restricted to iid Gaussian reference plus one fixed iid Gaussian step alternative and the frozen NIG block predictor.

candidate_new.mechanism: Precompute one standardized symmetric four-corner null mixture for the frozen NIG block predictor. If the continuum Theorem-4.7 constraint E_q[p_theta/p_rho]<=1 is certified for every theta in the Gaussian confidence rectangle, replace q/p_max by q/p_rho. This would be a common-increment conditional e-factor, preserve O(1) delayed-start compression, and pointwise dominate the r85 factor.
candidate_new.status: strong numerical RIPr candidate; exact continuum e-validity pending

frontier: Prove or interval-certify C(mu,sigma)=E_q[p_{mu,sigma}/p_rho]<=1 on the fixed standardized rectangle. Use symmetry to restrict mu>=0 and exploit the large observed interior margin; if only sup<=1+epsilon can be certified, scale by 1+epsilon and quantify whether pointwise dominance over UI survives.
Use the exact location-scale reduction to finish r85's KL>=1 miss-Chernoff continuum certificate without re-optimizing raw reference states.
If the four-corner factor becomes e-valid, quantify its latency gain with the same common-random detector paths. Safety should come from the continuum constraint, not simulation.
Replace the retained chi-square/normal/quadrature decimals with directed-rounding interval enclosures where possible.
exact_next_action: Write C(mu,sigma) in block mean and centered-SSE sufficient statistics for the four-corner p_rho. Prove corner maximality analytically or build a rigorous interval/transport cover of the standardized rectangle. If certified, promote the factor because q/p_rho>=q/p_max pointwise and the existing delayed-start architecture is unchanged. In parallel close the standardized r85 KL>=1 power surface; otherwise retain r85 and r84 unchanged.
